Efforts are being made by various stakeholders, including pharmaceutical manufacturers (both branded and generic) and other partners, to develop practical recommendations for the range of antiretroviral therapy (ART) formulations required to safely and effectively scale up ART for children. Simplified dosing regimens are being anticipated for pediatric formulations currently under development. For example, pediatric tablets or oral liquid formulations are being designed with specific drug strengths and dosing schedules based on weight bands. These weight bands include categories such as 3–<6 kg, 6–<10 kg, 10–<14 kg, 14–<20 kg, 20–<25 kg, and 25–<35 kg. The dosing is specified for morning (AM) and evening (PM) administration. 1. ABC/3TC/LPV/r (30 mg/15 mg/40 mg/10 mg granules): The dosing ranges from 2 granules in the AM and PM for the lowest weight band (3–<6 kg) to 6 granules in the AM and PM for the highest weight band (25–<35 kg). 2. DRV/r (120 mg/20 mg tablet): This formulation is recommended for children in higher weight bands, with dosing starting at 2 tablets in the AM and PM for 10–<14 kg and increasing to 4 tablets in the AM and PM for 25–<35 kg. 3. ABC/3TC/DTG (60 mg/30 mg/5 mg dispersible tablet): This formulation is identified as the most likely to deliver appropriate doses based on the best available data. Dosing starts at 3 tablets in the PM for 6–<10 kg and increases to 6 tablets in the PM for 20–<25 kg. The above formulations and dosing regimens are informed by the Pediatric Antiretroviral Drug Optimization (PADO) group, which prioritizes the development of pediatric ART formulations based on clinical evidence and pharmacokinetic data. References and Supporting Studies: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides a generic tool for ART dosing and has published consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and monitoring. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved specific drugs for treating infants and children with HIV, such as dolutegravir-based ART, which has been shown to be superior to NNRTI/PI-based regimens in children and adolescents. Pharmacokinetic studies, such as those on lopinavir/ritonavir and dolutegravir, have demonstrated the safety and efficacy of these drugs in pediatric populations, including those co-infected with tuberculosis. Clinical trials, such as the ODYSSEY trial, have provided evidence for simplified dolutegravir dosing in children weighing 20 kg or more. Studies like the PRINCE-2 trial have evaluated the safety and efficacy of atazanavir powder and ritonavir in HIV-1-infected infants and children aged 3 months to <11 years. Additional Resources: The Global Accelerator for Pediatric Formulations (GAP-f) initiative and the Pediatric ARV Procurement Working Group are actively involved in optimizing the availability and accessibility of pediatric ART formulations. The PADO 4 list prioritizes the most needed pediatric antiretroviral formulations, ensuring that the development pipeline aligns with clinical needs. These efforts collectively aim to improve the management of HIV in pediatric populations by ensuring access to safe, effective, and appropriately dosed ART formulations.
